quotes.quote: We evaluated the composition of immune infiltrates through microenvironment cell populations (MCP)-counter.
The MCP-counter package in R ( https://github.com ) was applied to evaluate the immune infiltration of each tissue sample from transcriptomic data.

G1.rationale: The principal result is produced by MCP-counter computation on public microarray data, which a third party can re-run.

quotes.quote: the red module had a strong positive correlation with the infiltrating levels of T cells and cytotoxic lymphocytes (r=0.90 and 0.84 respectively, all P<0.05)

G2.rationale: One principal quantitative result can be named: the correlation coefficients of the red module with T cells and cytotoxic lymphocytes.

quotes.quote: Three chips ( GSE47472 , GSE57691 , and GSE98278 ) related to AAA were annotated with Illumina HumanHT-12 v4.0 expression bead chip

G3.rationale: The listed GEO deposit files are the raw/non-normalized microarray inputs used for the analysis.

quotes.quote: the original datasets underwent background correction and quantile normalization by “Limma” package
Gene co-expression network was constructed by the weighted gene correlation network analysis (WGCNA) R software package
The criterion of co-expression weight >2.5 was used to select the candidate network.

G4.rationale: The published method describes normalization, WGCNA construction, and module selection sufficiently to implement without original code.

quotes.quote: All analyses were conducted with R version 3.5 ( https://www.r-project.org/ ) and its several open packages.

G5.rationale: The method uses R and open-source packages; no proprietary software is required.

specification.exact_target: Correlation of the red WGCNA module with infiltrating levels of T cells and cytotoxic lymphocytes in AAA, reported as r=0.90 and 0.84 respectively (all P<0.05).
specification.blind_target: The correlation between the most relevant WGCNA module and the infiltrating levels of T cells and cytotoxic lymphocytes in AAA tissues.
specification.target_location: Results, subsection 'AAA-related gene co-expression network construction', Figure 2C

location_quotes.quote: the red module had a strong positive correlation with the infiltrating levels of T cells and cytotoxic lymphocytes (r=0.90 and 0.84 respectively, all P<0.05) ( Figure 2C )

method_quotes.quote: Three chips ( GSE47472 , GSE57691 , and GSE98278 ) related to AAA were annotated with Illumina HumanHT-12 v4.0 expression bead chip
the original datasets underwent background correction and quantile normalization by “Limma” package
The MCP-counter package in R ( https://github.com ) was applied to evaluate the immune infiltration of each tissue sample from transcriptomic data.
Gene co-expression network was constructed by the weighted gene correlation network analysis (WGCNA) R software package
The criterion of co-expression weight >2.5 was used to select the candidate network.
We calculated the correlation between modules and AAA risk-related immune infiltrating components.

specification.input_notes: GEO accessions GSE47472, GSE57691, GSE98278; Illumina HumanHT-12 v4.0 expression bead chip. The RAW.tar files contain raw data; non-normalized data files are also listed but RAW.tar is sufficient for re-running normalization.

specification.comparison_metric: The reported correlation coefficients (r) are compared to the solver's computed correlation coefficients between the red module eigengene and MCP-counter scores for T cells and cytotoxic lymphocytes.
specification.numerical_agreement_criterion: Scalars within displayed rounding bin: r values rounded to two decimal places (0.90 and 0.84).
specification.specification_gaps: The exact method for selecting the red module (e.g., module-trait correlation threshold) is not fully specified; the MCP-counter version and parameters are not given; the WGCNA soft threshold selection details are incomplete; the handling of batch effects across datasets is not fully described.
specification.alternatives_considered: Other candidate targets included the differential infiltration P-values (Figure 1C) and the core gene correlation table (Table 2), but these are secondary to the principal module-trait correlation result.
